overview: Most of the week's snow favors the Northern Rockies and Cascades, with a Friday system spreading snow across Wyoming and Montana. The Northeast gets rain Thanksgiving night into Friday, and California's storm arrives around Sunday.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Storm systems keep moving through the Cascades. A Winter Storm Watch covers the North Cascades, including Washington Pass, from late Wednesday night into Thursday, with strong winds ahead of the front. Crystal Mountain leads the snow, with a 13-inch peak on Thursday and 39 inches for the week.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Dry, mild weather holds through Thanksgiving, with fog possible in valleys Wednesday morning. A system arrives Friday, bringing snow to western Wyoming through Saturday, and a band of snow may reach central Wyoming. Grand Targhee leads with a 22-inch peak on Friday. Forecasters say the snow band's position is still uncertain.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Cold, dry weather holds through early Thursday. A system brings mostly rain late Thanksgiving into Friday, with some freezing rain possible at the start, especially at higher elevations. Stowe and Jay Peak each peak at around 12 to 13 inches on Friday, and Stowe's 20-inch total is mostly from that day.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Rain and showers dominate the Coast Mountains. Whistler sees 11 inches on Wednesday and again on Thursday, and its total is 29 inches. Cypress Mountain gets most of its snow on Sunday.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: A front brings rain and light mountain snow through Wednesday morning, then dry weather returns. The Sierra sees little snow until Sunday, when a storm arrives. Palisades and Sugar Bowl each get 18 inches that day, while Kirkwood sees 11 inches. Forecasters expect an active pattern to return late this weekend.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Rain dominates early in the week, with a rising snow level Wednesday. Snow becomes more likely over the weekend. Whitewater peaks at 11 inches on Thursday and totals 17 inches, while RED Mountain gets 7 inches that day.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Mild, dry weather continues through Thanksgiving. Friday brings strong winds to the northern Front Range. Snow arrives in the northern mountains Friday and Saturday, with the Park Range most affected. Steamboat peaks at 11 inches Saturday, and Vail sees 9 inches that day. Forecasters have low confidence in exact amounts.

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Showers arrive Wednesday night and continue through Thursday. Big White peaks at 8 inches Thursday, and SilverStar gets 3 inches that day. Dry, mostly cloudy weather follows through the weekend.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
